inputs.scope: 45s synthetic Short retention curve (10 observed points)

assumptions: Dataset is explicitly labeled synthetic (FICTIONAL_OR_DEMO) for workflow demonstration.
limitations: Transcript alignment identifies possible contributors, not proven causation.
Stayed-to-watch and Engaged Views were not supplied in this export.
Single video (n=1); confirm pattern across a comparable multi-video cohort.

evidence.claim: Retention drops -18.0 pp between 12.0s and 16.0s (79.0% to 61.0%, 2.82x background drop slope) and spikes +49.5 pp to 108.5% at 28.0s.
Between 12.1s and 16.5s the caption contains a mid-video channel follow and link-in-bio CTA before the physics demonstration.

recommendation.action: Remove mid-video follow/bio CTA interruptions before the visual payoff on the next 3 comparable Shorts while preserving the slow-motion mechanism cutaway.
recommendation.rationale: The steepest non-spike drop (-18.0 pp at 12-16s) aligns with the mid-video CTA cue, whereas the cutaway beat at 22-28s coincides with a valid 108.5% rewatch spike.

cohort.comparability_note: Single synthetic video; compare against >=5 comparable Shorts in real channel usage.

findings: 12.0s-16.0s shows a -18.0 pp cliff (2.82x background slope) aligned with a mid-video CTA cue (possible contributor).
22.0s-28.0s rises +49.5 pp to 108.5% (valid rewatch spike; preserved without clamping).
28.0s-35.0s drop from 108.5% to 64.0% is flagged as a post-rewatch spike return rather than an early exit cliff.

experiment.hypothesis: Eliminating mid-video CTA interruptions before the visual payoff reduces 10-20s retention loss by >=8 pp while keeping the cutaway rewatch spike.
experiment.window: First 7 days post-publish across n>=3 comparable Shorts
experiment.controls: Same science demo pillar, ~45s duration, immediate visual hook, cutaway beat
